title: Unexpected Perturbations While Walking in Virtual Reality Environment
author: Uri Rosenblum
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bdjvi4n6

steps.title: Screen Participants
steps.instruction: Verify that participants meet the inclusion and exclusion criteria.

substeps.instruction: Confirm inclusion: Usually healthy, age 18-90.

Confirm exclusion: BMI > 30, orthopedic conditions affecting gait/balance (e.g., knee/hip replacement, ankle sprain, fracture), cognitive/psychiatric conditions (MMSE < 24), unstable ischemic heart disease or moderate to severe congestive heart failure, severe COPD, or neurological diseases associated with balance disorders (e.g., multiple sclerosis, myelopathy).

steps.title: Collect Participant Demographics
steps.instruction: Record the following participant data, using '555' for missing values:

substeps.instruction: Participant Code: Acronym of first and last name + last 3 digits of ID.
Sex: Male = 1, Female = 0.
Date of birth.
Height: In meters, two decimal places.
Leg length: Right limb from greater trochanter to floor in cm.
Weight: In kg.
BMI: Calculated as kg/m².
Years of Education.

steps.title: Perform Baseline Cognitive and Physical Assessments
steps.instruction: Conduct a battery of cognitive and mobility tests to establish baseline performance.

substeps.instruction: Record if the participant fell in the last year (1=yes, 0=no) and the number of falls.
Administer Mini Mental State Examination (MMSE) for older adults.
Perform Colors Trails Test (Part 1: connect numbers 1-25; Part 2: alternate between yellow and pink colors for numbers 1-25).
Perform Digit Span Test (repeat sequences forward and backward).
Administer NeuroTrax computerized battery of cognitive tests.
Perform Time Up and Go Test: Time the participant getting up from a chair, walking 3m, turning, and sitting back down (repeat twice at comfortable speed).
Perform 10 Meter Walking Test: Time the participant walking 10m in a 30m corridor (repeat 4 times).
Perform 10 Meter Walking Test with concurrent cognitive task: Subtract 7 from a random three-digit number while walking (repeat 4 times).
Perform 2 Minute Walking Test: Measure distance covered in 2 minutes walking back and forth in a 30m corridor.
Perform High Level Mobility Assessment Tool (HiMAT) tasks (fast walking, running, climbing stairs, jumping).
Perform Dynamic Gait Index (DGI) test (walking with head turns, changing directions, stepping over obstacles, turning, climbing stairs).

steps.title: Train Participant on Cognitive Task
steps.instruction: Teach the participant the Paced Auditory Serial Addition task.

substeps.instruction: Read a series of 15 numbers to the participant, one every 2 seconds.
Instruct the participant to add the numbers quietly in their head.
Require the participant to provide the final sum at the end.
Calculate the cognitive score for List 1 using the formula: 100-((|81-X|)/5.4)*6.66.

steps.title: Prepare Participant for Experiment
steps.instruction: Equip the participant and calibrate the tracking system.

substeps.instruction: Fit the participant with a safety harness and explain that they cannot fall.
Calibrate the Vicon motion capture system to the participant's range of motion.

steps.title: Acclimate Participant to Self-Paced Walking
steps.instruction: Introduce the participant to the self-paced treadmill paradigm.

substeps.instruction: Set treadmill to self-paced mode (motor speed functions based on instantaneous position and speed sampled via motion capture).
Have the participant maintain a comfortable walking speed for one minute.
Instruct the participant to dynamically modify gait speed (accelerate, decelerate, full stop, and resume).
Repeat until the participant is confident and transitions smoothly from standing to walking.

steps.title: Execute Perturbation Walking Trials
steps.instruction: Conduct walking trials in two VR scenes (park and hanging bridge) under single and dual-task conditions.

substeps.instruction: Randomize the order of scenes and conditions across participants.
Perform 4 trials per scene for both single-task (no cognitive load) and dual-task (concurrent arithmetic calculations) conditions.
Implement walking bouts of 10 and 5 minutes with rest between trials.
Ensure at least 30 seconds of baseline walking before and after every perturbation.

Trigger a random perturbation once steady-state velocity is reached, based on: (1) direction (medio-lateral or anterior-posterior), (2) gait phase (initial contact, mid-stance, or toe-off), and (3) reference foot (right or left).
For Medio-lateral perturbations (Level 12): Displace platform 15 cm left or right over 0.92 seconds; hold for 30 seconds; return to original position over 3 seconds.

For Anterior-posterior perturbations (Level 12): Fix treadmill speed to average self-paced speed 5 seconds prior to onset; reduce speed of one belt by 1.2 m/s with a deceleration of 5 m/s²; return to self-paced mode 3 seconds after the perturbation.

Detect gait phases using force plate (low-pass filter 5Hz, threshold 25N) and toe markers: Initial contact (>35N vertical force), mid-stance (200ms after initial contact), and toe-off (vertical force <35N on trailing limb).

steps.title: Capture Gait Parameters
steps.instruction: Record kinematic and temporal data during trials.

substeps.instruction: Obtain gait speed from the treadmill motor drive shaft encoder.
Obtain spatial-temporal parameters (step times, length, and width) from the Vicon motion capture system.
Detect gait cycle phases using foot markers and force plate data.
